comment: I graduated, but I still took the time to do this. I just don't want anyone to make the same mistakes I did. This class was brutal, with no way to know whether she would like or hate you after speaking in class. She is incredibly opinionated and allows that to influence your grade. Be wary of taking this class, and good luck if you do.

If you're scared of taking Dr. Henley, don't be. She's a very knowledgable and amiable professor. If you have a genuine interest in the material and are willing to read *well,* you'll be fine. It's not impossible to get an A. I spent no more than 2-4hrs a week, but if you're looking for a blow-off class, go somewhere else. Maybe Bschool.

Don't be scared of taking Dr. Henley. There is a learning curve for the course, but its not impossible to get an A. Reading well is crucial; still, I never spent more than 4hrs a week on homework for her class. She's a smart, amiable professor & you will learn a lot from the course. Take her if you truly care about the topic & you won't regret it.
By far the worst experience of my entire academic career.

By far the worst teacher I have ever had. I wish everyone luck if they have to take one of her classes; I know no one is willing to. I was also so excited to take Killers and Cults when I become a senior, but now I know that will be ruined because she teaches it. Take a class with 20 essays before this class.
No words. Will never take her class again.

I'm not sure what class some of the 5 star ratings took. It could not have been with Henley though. After talking with many, many, many fellow students not a single one had a good experience. I wish I took one of these 5 star rated classes. All I know is I will never take a class Henley teaches again.

I took her class as a freshman; currently a senior, I can say that Dr. Henley is by far one of the kindest and most considerate professors I've had at UR. Genuinely wants to get to know her students and see them succeed. The kind of professor you want to go to coffee and chat about life with. Absolutely not an impossible class to get an A in.

Very fun class. One of the few humanities/liberal arts classes I've taken without a ton of papers or a ton of exams; you record a speech, make a children's book explaining a topic, etc. Classroom discussions were interesting and challenging. Dr. Henley really encourages you to stray outside of your comfort zone (in a good way). 10/10 recommend.

Absolutely loved having Dr. Henley as a professor. She is widely considered to be one of the best leadership professors you can have, and I am so grateful I got to take a class with her. Super interesting and really challenges you to consider things deeply, while also being a relatively easy class to do well in.

It isn't an easy A, but the work teaches you a lot. It took some getting used to, but I love the class now. If you participate and try you best, it will be fine. The essays are a little difficult, but the professor gives good feedback and works with you to help you improve. The drastic difference between my first and second essay proves that.

Dr. Henley's Killers and Cults class is absolutely fantastic! The course content was extremely interesting (including a semester long scavenger hunt and a homicide investigation). Dr. Henley provides elaborate feedback that applies beyond the assignment. Despite writing a book, she was frequently available to meet and cares about student success.
worst class I took. very boring, almost fell asleep during class. grading system makes no sense, and getting above a B on any assigments is impossible. i don't recommend taking this class.

Just such a brutal, long, boring class. She gives out projects for us, then states they were the best things she has ever read, only to get a B. You really won't get higher than a B+ in this class, and something about her is off. She's nice, but classes feel extremely long, and there is so much reading.

I was excited about taking this class but I ended up having a bad experience. She does not care about her students success at all. She takes days to respond to emails and is very hard to meet with outside of class time. She is a harsh grader and claims that if you follow the syllabus you will receive a good grade but this is extremely inaccurate.

I dropped out Leadership school because of her. She claims her class is "ungraded" but then does not allow you to give yourself the grade you think you deserve. Incredibly inaccessible outside of class. She genuinely does not want to see her students to do well. Do not take her.

Dr. Henley is the least compassionate teacher I have ever had. I saw the good reviews and was excited to take this class. However, she repeatedly told us how she was writing a book, and her publishers made her rewrite it. This was her excuse for this semester being worse than others and why we got no feedback. She might be better next semester.

I had Henley for 201, and she was by far the WORST professor I have ever had. I wish I could write paragraphs. I wouldn't have been in Jepson if I knew she taught here. Her class is allegedly "self-graded." This is a total lie. The first exam average was a D-. Most insensitive professor ever. I would be a part-time student before taking her again.

utilize her office hours and send draft assignments to her a week in advance and she will give feedback.

communication matters

be respectful

Dr. Henley's class confirms the caliber of education to be found at Jepson. She is knowledgeable, clear, and personable. Her class was taught with intention and care, and she makes great efforts to respect every student's worldview and appreciates everyone's contributions. She grades assignments fairly and is happy to give feedback if you ask.

I was disappointed with Dr. Henley. She made it impossible to learn anything because every single class was about something different. "Class discussions" were through a discussion board, which was incredibly time-consuming and unhelpful. The assignments were meaningless and inconvenient; only group projects. She is insensitive and pretends to care

Dr. Henley is absolutely amazing! She is very knowledgeable about what she teaches and cares very much about her students. She is an incredible person and inspiring professor. This class is what made me want to become a part of Jepson in the first place, and I am very grateful for what I learned in this class.

Dr. Henley is the best professor and mentor I have ever had! She is so considerate and kind. She has clear grading criteria and flexibility in the assignments to suit whatever interests or strengths you may have. While the class was difficult, I could not have asked for a more accommodating professor. Definitely take her class if possible!

Dr. Henley was amazing. Yes, her intro class is hard and she is a different grader than I've ever had (to get an A, you must be exceptional by her standards), but she was such a great professor. She splits classes by lectures and group activities. Her history background really helps. Never bored during a lecture, she she just knows what she's doing

Dr. Henley is a very unique and amazing Professor in Jepson... She cares about the topics and has a passion for her students to understand and appreciate them too. She is very intelligent and each assignment is interesting and has a purpose, there are minimal tests (if any), lots of readings, and more comprehensive and enjoyable projects.

Dr. Henley has a very unique approach to teaching. Her grading criteria make all assignments low stakes. Students have a variety of options based on what interests them most. Each week, she lectures one day and does group work the other day. She claims to hate lecturing but is very inspirational. Her feedback is very helpful as is her teaching.
